intro: A fiancé or proposed civil partner visa lets you come to the UK to marry or form a civil partnership with your British or settled partner. After the wedding, you switch to a spouse visa without leaving the UK. We prepare your fiancé visa application and check every document before it goes to the Home Office.
eligibility: You plan to marry or form a civil partnership within the visa period
You have met each other in person
You meet the financial and English language requirements
You can show your wedding plans are genuine

faqs.q: Can I work on a fiancé visa?
faqs.a: No. You cannot work on a fiancé visa. You can work once you switch to a spouse visa after the wedding.

faqs.q: What happens if the wedding is delayed?
faqs.a: You must marry within the 6 months. If the wedding can’t go ahead in time, talk to us straight away about your options.

faqs.q: How long does a fiancé visa take?
faqs.a: Applications from outside the UK are usually decided within about 12 weeks.

sections.heading: What a fiancé(e) visa allows
sections.text:
A fiancé(e) or proposed civil partner visa lets you come to the UK to marry or enter a civil partnership with your British or settled partner. It lasts 6 months, and you must marry within that time.

After the wedding, you switch to a spouse visa from inside the UK without leaving. You can't work while on a fiancé(e) visa.

sections.heading: Requirements for a fiancé(e) visa
sections.text:
You need to show:
- You and your partner are both 18 or over and have met in person
- Your relationship is genuine and you plan to live together permanently in the UK
- You plan to marry within 6 months, with evidence such as a booked venue, registry office correspondence or wedding plans
- Your partner meets the financial requirement, usually £29,000 a year
- You meet the English language requirement at A1 level
- You will have suitable accommodation

Any previous marriages must have ended legally, with divorce or death certificates as evidence.

sections.heading: Fiancé visa or spouse visa?
sections.text: If you can marry outside the UK first, applying directly for a spouse visa is often simpler and cheaper, as you only make one application before arriving. A fiancé(e) visa suits couples who want to marry in the UK. We'll help you compare costs and timings.
